title: The key picks the partition; the group gives each partition one reader
caption: Topic 'orders' with 3 partitions and consumer group 'billing' with 2 members. Order is kept inside a partition, never across them.

steps.text: The producer computes hash(order_id) % 3 for every record. Every event of order 17 lands in p0, in the order it was written.
Each partition is an append-only file. A record's offset (0, 1, 2…) is its permanent position in that partition.
Group 'billing' splits the partitions: c1 owns p0 and p1, c2 owns p2. Each partition has exactly one reader in the group, so per-key order survives.
Each consumer pulls from its committed offset. A third consumer would get p0 or p1 from c1; a fourth would sit idle, because there are only 3 partitions.
